mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of such rate increase episodes, or the 20-day IC is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting equity market optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >2% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: IC for 60-day horizon remains negative (<0.01) or positive returns occur <40% of the time in such labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests weakening demand for manufactured goods, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns (when applicable) are non-negative in >80% of such episodes, or the 5-day IC is positive (>0.02).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three months indicates a cooling inflation environment, reducing policy uncertainty and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such episodes, or the 20-day IC is negative (<-0.03).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% while UNRATE remains below 4%, it indicates a potential shift toward accommodative policy, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: IC for 20-day horizon is negative (> -0.05) in >70% of such policy shifts.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising while UNRATE steady), the S&P 500 exhibits negative 5-day forward returns as higher discount rates depress expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months with UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >75% of such tightening episodes, or the 5-day IC exceeds 0.04.
